verdicts.reason: Directly formalizes the directional memory retrieval constraint where previously consolidated knowledge impairs the acquisition or recall of new information, providing the psychological foundation for CognitiveInterferenceGate.
Models the converse memory vulnerability where freshly encoded knowledge disrupts or overwrites pre-existing stored traces, governing retention policies and consolidation schedules.
Defines the temporal attenuation and decay of memory trace accessibility over time, directly modeling the power-law decay of base-level activation in ACT-R retrieval.
Captures the quantitative savings metric of latent memory retention, measuring reacquisition speed and demonstrating structural persistence below the explicit retrieval threshold.
Defines the pathological failure of declarative consolidation from working memory to long-term storage, delineating architectural boundaries between buffer state and persistent memory.
Defines the selective disruption of consolidated historical memory traces, separating retrieval indexing failures from encoding deficits.
Formalizes the intentional semantic linking of novel items to established conceptual structures, representing the active procedural mechanism of memory consolidation.
Captures reconstructive memory distortion caused by post-event misleading cues, acting as an essential guardrail for epistemic judgment and memory integrity.
Represents the physical or neural representational unit of memory storage, defining the fundamental substrate of declarative and nondeclarative persistence.
Formulates the distributed fault-tolerance principle of memory substrates where undamaged network components compensate for localized failures.
